headline: Regional Forest Passes and Seasonal Park Reservations
reservation: While the town itself is open, nearby attractions like Echo Lake State Park may require advanced day-use reservations during peak summer. White Mountain National Forest trailheads require a parking fee or pass. Always check the New Hampshire State Parks site for the latest booking requirements at specific landmarks.

days.title: Valley Views and Heritage Rails
days.start: Suggested: 9:00 AM from North Conway Village

stops.name: Conway Scenic Railroad
stops.detail: Observe the Mount Washington Valley from a heritage train departing from the historic 1874 station.

stops.name: Cathedral Ledge
stops.detail: Drive or hike to the summit for a bird’s-eye view of the Saco River Valley and Echo Lake below.

days.driving: Walking within the village; 15-minute drive to ledges; conditions vary by season.
days.note: Cathedral Ledge road is seasonal; check for winter closures if visiting for ice climbing.

days.title: The Scenic Kancamagus Highway

stops.name: Lower Falls
stops.detail: Visit this popular rocky stretch of the Swift River for scenic photography and river air.

stops.name: Sabbaday Falls
stops.detail: Walk the easy gravel path to see a multi-tiered waterfall and a distinct rock flume.

days.driving: Allow 4 hours for a round-trip drive with frequent scenic stops; conditions vary.
days.note: There is no fuel or cell service on the 34-mile stretch of the Kancamagus Highway.

days.title: Mountain Notches and Waterfalls

stops.name: Diana's Baths
stops.detail: Follow the short trail to a series of cascading pools and potholes along Lucy Brook.

stops.name: Crawford Notch State Park
stops.detail: Drive north to see the rugged cliffs of the notch and the impressive Silver Cascade waterfall.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours for regional transit; mountain weather can change rapidly.
days.note: Diana's Baths parking is extremely limited; arrive very early or choose a weekday visit.

intel.title: Digital Payment at Trailheads
intel.text: Many Forest Service sites now use digital payment apps or require exact cash for envelopes. Ensure you have the Recreation.gov app downloaded before leaving town.

intel.title: Valley vs. Mountain Service
intel.text: Village connectivity is reliable, but signals drop immediately upon entering the National Forest. Map your route to notches and trailheads while still in North Conway.

intel.title: Gateway Hubs
intel.text: North Conway is the primary fuel hub for the eastern White Mountains. Fill your tank before heading west toward Lincoln or north toward the Presidential Range.

intel.title: Leaf Peeping Traffic
intel.text: During peak October weekends, travel times on Route 16 can triple. Plan midweek visits if your schedule allows for a quieter foliage experience.

intel.title: Mud Season Constraints
intel.text: High-elevation trails remain wet and fragile through May. Stick to hardened surfaces or valley walks to protect the environment during the spring thaw.

plan.arrival: Fly into Portland (PWM), pick up your rental, and drive west through the scenic Sebago Lake region. Settle into your North Conway base and explore the Main Street shops.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are suitable for main roads; however, winter travel requires AWD/4WD and winter tires. Check rental policies for ski-rack availability.
plan.goldenHour: Cathedral Ledge offers a panoramic sunset view over the valley, though the access road closes at dusk; verify times locally.
